item.title: Terminal-Bench Science: Four Accepted Tasks in v0.1
item.description: Project: Terminal-Bench Science, a benchmark for AI agents working through computational tasks in the natural sciences. Release: v0.1.0, released in August 2026. Contribution: I was a main contributor to Terminal-Bench Science v0.1. Four tasks I contributed to were accepted into v0.1. Overview Link to heading Terminal-Bench Science studies whether AI systems can work through realistic scientific-computing workflows in a terminal environment. The benchmark is about more than producing code that looks plausible: an agent must understand the scientific setting, carry out the workflow, and produce a result that can be checked.

item.title: Exact lower bounds on the non-convergence probability of probabilistic direct search
item.description: Status: Work in progress, 2026. This note studies a quantitative aspect of non-convergence in probabilistic direct search. The goal is to better understand how likely certain failure patterns can be, and how their scale may be described. The manuscript is still being prepared, so I am keeping the technical details intentionally brief here. Coming soon.

item.title: Non-convergence analysis of probabilistic direct search
item.description: Paper: C. Huang and Z. Zhang. Non-convergence analysis of probabilistic direct search. Preprint, 2026. PDF | Poster (PRSC 2024) Overview Link to heading This paper establishes the non-convergence theory for probabilistic direct search. Probabilistic direct search is a class of derivative-free optimization methods that uses randomized polling directions to improve efficiency. Existing convergence theory shows that the algorithm converges when the polling direction sets satisfy a probabilistic descent assumption. We study a natural question: how will the algorithm behave when these assumptions are not met?

item.title: Error analysis of finite difference scheme for American option pricing under regime-switching with jumps
item.description: Paper: C. Huang, H. Song, J. Yang, and B. Zhou. Error analysis of finite difference scheme for american option pricing under regime-switching with jumps. J. Comput. Appl. Math., accepted for publication, 2023. PDF Overview Link to heading This paper develops an efficient numerical method for pricing American options under regime-switching jump-diffusion models (Merton’s and Kou’s models). The problem is formulated as a free-boundary problem or complementarity problem with integral and differential terms on an unbounded domain.

2022–present, PhD student in Applied Optimization and Optimal Control, Department of Applied Mathematics, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong SAR, China. Supervised by Prof. Zaikun Zhang and Prof. Xiaojun Chen. Funded by the Research Grants Committee (RGC) of Hong Kong under the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme (HKPFS). 2018–2022, BSc in Information and Computing Science (Computational Mathematics), School of Mathematics, Jilin University, Changchun, China.
